searches.result: The standard normal law and distributional convergence support asymptotic calibration after a quantile/tail bridge, but they do not establish the limit of this statistic.

library_audit.gap: Construct the standard-normal upper-tail a critical value and derive the rejection-probability limit from the paper's null CLT and valid studentization assumptions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Set z_i=(x_i-mu_X) times [y_i-mu_Y-inner(x_i-mu_X,beta0)] using actual population expectations, then use the regression model to obtain inner(x_i-mu_X,beta-beta0)+epsilon_i in the residual. Centered covariance entries and zero cross moments with epsilon give E z_i=Sigma_X*(beta-beta0), subject to integrability; the totalized integral must not hide missing moments. This applies to iid population-centered scores, not the practical scores sharing xbar,ybar. Sigma_X may be singular under the upper-eigenvalue assumptions, so the identity alone does not make mu=0 equivalent to beta=beta0.
